title: Keep Unicode case-insensitive page search in original text coordinates
problem: read_web_page computes find position in casefolded text but slices original text with that index. Case folding can expand characters. For plain text consisting of 600 sharp-s characters followed by NEEDLE, find=needle reports a match but starts the excerpt at 700 instead of 100, excluding the match.
acceptance_criteria: Case-insensitive find locates matches using Unicode casefold semantics while computing offset and excerpt in original text coordinates, retaining up to 500 original characters before the match.

Preserve expansion-aware matching (for example STRASSE matches Straße), first-match selection, and matches inside an expanded character; the original character containing the folded match is the start.
ASCII matching, no-match behavior, explicit offset pagination, and the existing 100000-character text bound and 8000-character excerpt size remain unchanged.
Add concise async standard-library unittest regression coverage using synthetic text, mock HTTP transport, and a stub resolver. No network or model calls.
Keep changes limited to search-coordinate calculation and one new test module. Preserve parser behavior, safe URL handling, DNS pinning, response shape, dependencies, and existing tests.
exclusions: No UI changes, new dependencies, alternative search semantics, page-fetch redesign, or edits to other target files.
